reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an analysis of Terra/Luna's stablecoin mechanics, upgrades, and investment outlook, while attributing the 25.39% staking figure to Binance. The creator expresses a bullish opinion and discusses buying, burning, and staking, but the transcript does not direct viewers to a creator-controlled destination or request money or personal data.

citations.quote: Today's our today's topic is Tera You know it by name as Luna
the future of stable coin
this is my theory after researching this coin
when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%

opening.argument: The video links a concrete return claim to a concrete viewer action: staking Luna. The promised reward is not merely a general market observation; the wording presents staking as the route to receiving 25.39%. The supporting Binance material reinforces the same action-return pairing, describing LUNA staking with an APY up to 25.39% and identifying a locked staking format. That combination gives viewers a clear participation pathway while emphasizing an unusually high passive return.

citations.quote: when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video analysis does not remove the solicitation embedded in its most actionable claim. The speaker does not merely mention staking as background; the statement directly pairs staking Luna with a specific reward. Nor does attribution to Binance make the promotion neutral: the video repeats the return as a reason the project is attractive and says the project is good for the long term.

citations.quote: when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%
this coin's project is very good for the long term

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quote establishes that a staking reward was discussed, but it does not establish that the creator promised, controlled, or guaranteed that return. The visual source identifies Binance as the service and describes an APY of up to 25.39%, with a locked, first-come, first-served format. That is attributed platform information, not a creator-operated payment or collection scheme.

citations.quote: bynes announced when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%

opening.argument: Several risk signals converge around the staking pitch. The return is a specific 25.39% figure, the video calls the project strong for the long term, and the referenced staking offer is visibly presented as high-yield and locked. The surrounding message also predicts that Luna's price will rise as supply decreases, adding an appreciation narrative to the passive-return narrative. Together, these features can make participation appear unusually attractive while leaving the viewer without a balanced account of loss, lockup, or return uncertainty.

citations.quote: when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%
this coin's project is very good for the long term
in case of burning of any coin, the circulating supply is less and price will go up automatically

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference framing isolates the educational vocabulary while minimizing the risk signals actually presented. A precise APY, a locked-staking format, and repeated claims that scarcity will make the price rise are not necessary to explain stablecoin mechanics. They are persuasive reasons to participate, especially when the conclusion calls the project strong for the long term.

citations.quote: this coin's project is very good for the long term
the circulating supply is less and price will go up automatically

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are risk indicators only if the presentation conceals the nature of the offer, and the evidence does not show that. The return is attributed to Binance, while the video also explains the mechanism and frames its conclusion as the speaker's theory. The statements do not guarantee profit or establish that losses, lockup terms, or uncertainty were hidden.

citations.quote: this is my theory after researching this coin
announced when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39

opening.argument: Although packaged as explanation, the video functions as promotion by repeatedly steering attention toward participation and upside. It describes staking as producing a 25.39% reward, says Luna's price will rise automatically when supply falls, and concludes that the project is strong for the long term. The title itself calls the project bullish and advertises an upcoming update. This is more than detached reporting: the educational discussion is arranged to make staking and holding the token look attractive.

citations.quote: when stacking luna, you will get a reward of 25.39%
price will go up automatically
this coin's project is very good for the long term
bullish project

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the absence of a direct creator-controlled destination as dispositive, but promotion can operate through persuasion toward a third-party staking venue. The video supplies both the benefit and the favorable conclusion: staking is tied to 25.39%, and the project is described as strong long term. Calling that a theory does not neutralize its directional effect.

this is my theory after researching this coin
this coin's project is very good for the long term

The video identifies the source of the return as Binance and discusses Terra's mechanics, upgrades, and applications rather than directing viewers to send money or personal information to the speaker. The title's word 'bullish' signals an opinion; it does not establish a deceptive investment scheme.
